common_name: Supertunia Black Cherry Petunia (Deep Near-Black Cherry-Red Spreading Petunia)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Supertunia Black Cherry bears deep, near-black cherry-red flowers on a vigorous, mounding, trailing plant.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Supertunia Black Cherry produces an abundance of deep, near-black cherry-red flowers over a vigorous, mounding, trailing plant, one of the darkest colors available in the Supertunia series, providing a dramatic contrast against brighter companion annuals in mixed containers and landscape beds. It is largely self-cleaning, needing little deadheading to keep flowering heavily from spring through frost. Regular fertilizing supports its vigorous growth and continuous bloom, and a mid-season trim can rejuvenate the planting if it becomes overly leggy in the heat of summer.

common_name: Wave Purple Petunia (Classic Original Spreading Groundcover Petunia)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Purple Wave was the original spreading, groundcover-type petunia that launched the entire Wave series.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, giving it ample room to spread. Purple Wave was the groundbreaking original introduction that launched the entire Wave petunia series, spreading rapidly into a low, dense, weed-suppressing mat covered in vivid purple flowers from spring through frost, unlike the more upright, mounding habit of traditional petunias. Its vigorous, low-growing spread makes it especially effective as a flowering groundcover, spilling over walls, or filling large landscape beds and containers. It is largely self-cleaning and needs little deadheading, though a mid-season trim can rejuvenate the planting if it becomes overly leggy in the heat of summer.

common_name: Cooler Vinca (Pastel-Colored Compact Annual Vinca Series)

planting.note: Transplant into warm soil a week or two after the last frost once nights stay reliably above 60F; Cooler is a compact vinca series in soft pastel colors, one of the older widely grown seed strains.

directions: Transplant into warm, well-drained soil in full sun. Cooler bears large, flat flowers in soft pastel shades of pink, white, and lavender, often with a contrasting darker eye, on a compact, uniform plant that has long been a standard bedding vinca strain before the introduction of newer disease-resistant series. Once established it is remarkably drought- and heat-tolerant, blooming continuously from late spring through the first frost with almost no deadheading required. Avoid overhead irrigation late in the day and ensure good drainage, since vinca is susceptible to soilborne disease in consistently wet soil.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Vinca Disease Resistance Trials
